compositions.name: Rule of thirds
compositions.name_th: กฎสามส่วน
compositions.what: Divide the frame by two vertical and two horizontal lines; place the subject, eyes or horizon on a line or an intersection (power point).
compositions.why_it_works: Craft heuristic. It reliably avoids dead-centre static placement and leaves look/lead room (curriculum-03). There is no strong perceptual evidence that thirds placement itself is preferred; its value is as a quick off-centre starting point.
how_to_apply: Decide the single focal point
Put it on the intersection on the side opposite to where it looks or moves
Place horizon on a horizontal third, not the centre
Use the empty two-thirds for context or text
compositions.good_example: Customer trying on round gold glasses, eyes on the upper third line, face on the left third, looking right into blurred shop shelves.
compositions.bad_example: Every product and every face dropped onto an intersection automatically, so a whole carousel looks the same and faces look into the near edge.
compositions.fix: Choose placement from intent: give look room, or centre deliberately when symmetry serves the message.
compositions.when_to_break: Hero product and logos (centre), symmetry, 9:16 (vertical centre axis + horizontal thirds), 2.39:1 where thirds lines sit too far apart (curriculum-03).
compositions.focal_point_strategy: One subject at one power point; secondary element at the diagonal opposite point.
compositions.viewing_path: Power point → along gaze direction → secondary point or text area.
compositions.aspect_ratio_notes: 16:9 works best; 1:1 fine; 4:5 use upper third for eyes; 9:16 keep subject near vertical centre (right side collides with UI buttons) and use horizontal thirds; 21:9 lines too far apart.
compositions.negative_space_use: The two empty thirds hold context, eye room or headline.
compositions.depth_layers: Optional; FG element on the opposite third adds depth.
ai_prompt_phrases: her face on the left third of the frame, looking toward empty space on the right
horizon on the lower third line
subject placed off-centre in the left third
compositions.ai_pitfalls: Typing 'rule of thirds' alone gives random placement; say what goes where (curriculum-03). Image models default to a centred, mid-sized subject; position words are often ignored, more so at low step counts (FLUX schnell). Workarounds: state position in plain words early in the prompt (subject → framing → light, curriculum-03), generate at the final aspect ratio, use img2img from a rough layout sketch or HTML block-out (tools/flux.py --init --denoise 0.6-0.8), outpaint/extend canvas to move the subject off-centre, or generate wider and crop after.

overlay_guide.note: Normalised 0-1, origin top-left.

compositions.name: Golden ratio (phi grid)
compositions.name_th: สัดส่วนทองคำ
compositions.what: Divide the frame at 0.382 / 0.618 (phi grid) instead of thirds.
compositions.why_it_works: Weak/mixed evidence. Claims that the golden ratio is innately preferred or underlies famous works are largely myths (Parthenon ≈ 9:4, Vitruvius never mentions it — curriculum-03 citing PetaPixel/Photography Life). Use it as another off-centre grid only, never as a reason a picture is good.
how_to_apply: Use the phi lines as a slightly more central alternative to thirds
Place the subject on a 0.382/0.618 line
Check after platform crop; the ~5% difference from thirds often vanishes
compositions.good_example: Frame resting on sand slightly left of centre at x≈0.382, sky gradient above for a headline.
compositions.bad_example: Drawing a spiral and grid over a finished image to 'prove' it is beautiful.
compositions.fix: Pick placement by intent; treat phi as an option among grids.
compositions.when_to_break: Almost always optional; skip it when thirds or centre fits.
compositions.viewing_path: Like thirds but closer to centre.
compositions.aspect_ratio_notes: Differences from thirds shrink with width: on 1080 px ≈ 52 px (curriculum-03); in 9:16 use horizontal phi lines only.
compositions.negative_space_use: Larger 0.618 area holds context/text.
compositions.depth_layers: Not inherent.
ai_prompt_phrases: subject placed slightly left of centre, about 40 percent from the left edge
compositions.ai_pitfalls: 'golden ratio composition' does nothing verifiable in prompts (curriculum-03); give explicit positions. Workarounds: state position in plain words early in the prompt (subject → framing → light, curriculum-03), generate at the final aspect ratio, use img2img from a rough layout sketch or HTML block-out (tools/flux.py --init --denoise 0.6-0.8), outpaint/extend canvas to move the subject off-centre, or generate wider and crop after.

overlay_guide.note: Phi grid; compare against thirds 0.333/0.667.

compositions.name: Golden spiral
compositions.name_th: เกลียวทองคำ
compositions.what: A logarithmic spiral growing by phi each quarter turn, used as a curving path that ends at the focal point.
compositions.why_it_works: Weak evidence; overlays after the fact suffer confirmation bias because the spiral can be moved, scaled and flipped to fit almost anything (curriculum-03, Fstoppers). The useful part is the craft idea of a curving path coiling into the subject.
how_to_apply: Design a curved flow (S-curve, arc of objects) that tightens toward the subject
Place the subject at the spiral's eye
Never chase the exact curve
compositions.good_example: Wave line on a beach curving from the bottom right into a pair of sunglasses at the upper left power point.
compositions.bad_example: Spiral drawn over a random photo with claims it explains the appeal.
compositions.fix: Describe the curve and the end point in words; use s_curve_flow logic.
compositions.when_to_break: Graphic layouts, symmetry, most text-led posts.
compositions.focal_point_strategy: Subject at the tight end of the curve.
compositions.viewing_path: Wide end → along the curve → eye of the spiral.
compositions.aspect_ratio_notes: Natural in 3:2/16:9; squashed in 1:1; vertical in 9:16 (rotate 90°).
compositions.negative_space_use: The wide outer part can be quiet space.
compositions.depth_layers: Curve may run from FG to BG.
ai_prompt_phrases: a curving line of shells leading from the lower right corner to the glasses at the upper left
compositions.ai_pitfalls: Models cannot follow 'golden spiral'; describe the actual curved elements. Workarounds: state position in plain words early in the prompt (subject → framing → light, curriculum-03), generate at the final aspect ratio, use img2img from a rough layout sketch or HTML block-out (tools/flux.py --init --denoise 0.6-0.8), outpaint/extend canvas to move the subject off-centre, or generate wider and crop after.

overlay_guide.note: Draw any of 8 orientations; eye at a phi intersection. Display as a teaching aid, not a score.

compositions.name: Leading lines
compositions.name_th: เส้นนำสายตา
compositions.what: Lines in the scene (roads, rails, shelves, counter edges, shadows) that run toward the subject.
compositions.why_it_works: Evidence-backed in part: edges and orientation are strong low-level saliency features (Itti1998), and Gestalt continuity groups lines into paths (Wagemans2012). That they literally steer gaze is craft-supported and plausible.
how_to_apply: Find or add lines converging on the subject
Start lines at frame edges/corners
Avoid lines that run out of frame past the subject
Diagonals add energy
compositions.good_example: Floor tiles and a display counter converge on a teen sitting in the eye-test chair (curriculum-03 example).
compositions.bad_example: A strong road line leading out of the frame away from the person.
compositions.fix: Reposition the camera so lines meet at the subject, or block exiting lines with an object.
compositions.when_to_break: Minimal or flat graphic posts where lines add clutter.
compositions.aspect_ratio_notes: 9:16: vertical lines/paths from bottom to the face; 16:9: horizontal or one-point; 1:1: diagonals.
compositions.negative_space_use: Lines can cross empty space to connect it to the subject.
compositions.depth_layers: Lines receding from FG to BG create depth.
ai_prompt_phrases: the lines of the wooden counter lead the eye toward the glasses
one-point perspective, lines converging on the subject
compositions.ai_pitfalls: Models add lines but rarely aim them at the subject. Use one-point perspective wording, or a layout sketch with img2img. Workarounds: state position in plain words early in the prompt (subject → framing → light, curriculum-03), generate at the final aspect ratio, use img2img from a rough layout sketch or HTML block-out (tools/flux.py --init --denoise 0.6-0.8), outpaint/extend canvas to move the subject off-centre, or generate wider and crop after.

overlay_guide.note: Example corner-to-centre lines; analyze tool should detect actual lines (Hough) and test whether they converge within 0.1 of the focal point.

compositions.name: Symmetry
compositions.name_th: สมมาตร
compositions.what: Mirror balance around a central axis; subject on the centre line.
compositions.why_it_works: Symmetry is detected rapidly and is a strong Gestalt grouping/figure cue (Wagemans2012). Emotional effect (formal, calm, comic or uncanny) is context-driven craft (curriculum-03: Kubrick vs Wes Anderson).
how_to_apply: Align the camera exactly on the axis
Level horizon
Match left and right elements
Add one small asymmetry only if it is the point
compositions.good_example: Frontal view of glasses centred on a symmetrical display shelf, soft light both sides.
compositions.bad_example: Almost-symmetrical shot 3° off-axis — reads as a mistake.
compositions.fix: Commit fully: perfect alignment or clearly asymmetric.
compositions.when_to_break: When you need motion or tension; when the subject's gaze needs room.
compositions.viewing_path: Centre → out to symmetric pairs → back to centre.
compositions.aspect_ratio_notes: Strong in 1:1 and 9:16 (centre axis fits UI); in 16:9 wide sides become decoration.
compositions.negative_space_use: Equal margins.
compositions.depth_layers: One-point perspective adds depth.
ai_prompt_phrases: perfectly symmetrical frontal composition, subject on the exact centre line
one-point perspective, mirror symmetry
compositions.ai_pitfalls: Models produce near-symmetry with mismatched details (two different temple arms); inspect. Use mirror-flip of one half in post if needed.

overlay_guide.note: Score left/right mirror difference.

compositions.name: Asymmetrical balance
compositions.name_th: สมดุลแบบไม่สมมาตร
compositions.what: A large or dark mass on one side balanced by a smaller but brighter, more saturated or more interesting element on the other.
compositions.why_it_works: Arnheim1974 describes visual weight from size, colour, position, isolation and interest, with a lever-like effect from distance to centre. Evidence for exact weights is limited; treat as craft informed by perception theory.
how_to_apply: Place the heavy element nearer centre
Place the light element further out
Use colour or brightness to boost the small element
Check by squinting
compositions.good_example: Dark wooden cabinet filling the left, a small bright red frame on the right third.
compositions.bad_example: All heavy objects on one side, empty other side with no counterweight.
compositions.fix: Add a small accent opposite, or shift masses.
compositions.when_to_break: When unease is intended (intentional imbalance, Mr. Robot short-siding, curriculum-03).
compositions.aspect_ratio_notes: Easier in wide ratios; 9:16 balances top vs bottom.
compositions.negative_space_use: Space around the light element increases its weight (isolation).
compositions.depth_layers: Masses can sit on different planes.
ai_prompt_phrases: a large dark cabinet on the left balanced by a small bright red pair of glasses on the right
compositions.ai_pitfalls: Models drift to centring the main object; state both masses and sides. Workarounds: state position in plain words early in the prompt (subject → framing → light, curriculum-03), generate at the final aspect ratio, use img2img from a rough layout sketch or HTML block-out (tools/flux.py --init --denoise 0.6-0.8), outpaint/extend canvas to move the subject off-centre, or generate wider and crop after.

overlay_guide.note: Compute weighted centroid of saliency/contrast; balanced if within ±0.08 of 0.5 horizontally.

compositions.name: Radial
compositions.name_th: รัศมีจากศูนย์กลาง
compositions.what: Elements radiate from or circle around a centre point.
compositions.why_it_works: Converging/ radiating lines and concentric shapes point to the centre (Gestalt continuity, Wagemans2012); strong centre pull. Specific emotional effects are craft.
how_to_apply: Put the subject at the hub
Arrange spokes evenly
Keep spokes simpler than the hub
compositions.good_example: Frames arranged like petals around one featured pair on a table, top-down.
compositions.bad_example: Uneven spokes and a weak centre — eye has nowhere to land.
compositions.fix: Strengthen hub contrast; even out spokes.
compositions.when_to_break: When the story is about one direction of movement.
compositions.aspect_ratio_notes: Best 1:1; in 9:16 put hub in upper-middle; in 16:9 spokes stretch.
compositions.negative_space_use: Space between spokes.
compositions.depth_layers: Usually flat (top-down) or tunnel-like.
ai_prompt_phrases: eyeglass frames arranged in a radial pattern around one central pair, top-down view
compositions.ai_pitfalls: Models struggle with exact counts and even spacing; build in HTML from cutouts instead.

overlay_guide.note: Spokes every 30°.

compositions.name: Triangular
compositions.name_th: สามเหลี่ยม
compositions.what: Three key points (faces, objects) form a triangle; stable when based at the bottom.
compositions.why_it_works: Craft (classical painting, triangle staging in film — curriculum-03). Closure groups three points into one shape (Gestalt).
how_to_apply: Pick three elements
Vary their depth and height
Make the apex the most important
Avoid a flat line-up
compositions.good_example: Mother FG left, son MG centre, optometrist BG right — all faces visible (curriculum-03).
compositions.bad_example: Three people in a row at equal height.
compositions.fix: Stagger heights and distances.
compositions.when_to_break: Single-subject frames; deliberately confrontational line-ups.
compositions.focal_point_strategy: Apex or the most lit vertex.
compositions.viewing_path: Vertex → vertex → vertex, ending at apex.
compositions.aspect_ratio_notes: Wide ratios allow wide base; 9:16 use tall triangle.
compositions.negative_space_use: Space inside the triangle connects the elements.
compositions.depth_layers: Natural FG/MG/BG staging.
ai_prompt_phrases: triangle staging: one person in the foreground left, one in the centre midground, one in the background right
compositions.ai_pitfalls: Models line characters up side by side; specify FG/MG/BG positions explicitly.

overlay_guide.note: Example upright triangle.

compositions.name: Diagonal
compositions.name_th: แนวทแยง
compositions.what: Main lines or the subject axis run corner to corner.
compositions.why_it_works: Arnheim1974 discusses oblique orientation as dynamic tension compared with stable verticals/horizontals; widely used craft. Effects on viewers are not precisely quantified.
how_to_apply: Align the subject or a line along a diagonal
Start in a corner
Avoid slight accidental tilt
compositions.good_example: Temple arm of a frame running from lower left to upper right in a macro.
compositions.bad_example: Horizon tilted 2°, looking like an error.
compositions.fix: Commit to a clear angle (≥ 15°) or level it.
compositions.when_to_break: Calm, formal, trustworthy messages.
compositions.focal_point_strategy: End of the diagonal or a point on it.
compositions.aspect_ratio_notes: 1:1 prevents flat feel (curriculum-03); 9:16 steeper diagonal.
compositions.negative_space_use: Triangles of space either side.
compositions.depth_layers: Diagonal receding into depth adds perspective.
ai_prompt_phrases: the glasses placed diagonally from the lower left to the upper right corner
dynamic diagonal composition
compositions.ai_pitfalls: Models default to horizontal product placement; rotate the cutout in HTML or describe the diagonal explicitly.

overlay_guide.note: Main diagonals; also baroque/sinister diagonals.

compositions.name: Centred
compositions.name_th: วางกลาง
compositions.what: Subject at the centre of the frame.
compositions.why_it_works: Craft: centring is correct for hero products, logos and symmetrical subjects (curriculum-03) and reads as stable, direct and confident (Arnheim1974 treats the centre as the most balanced position). A general tendency of viewers to look at image centres is often reported, but no source for it is cited here.
how_to_apply: Centre the subject exactly
Simplify background
Use symmetry or a frame to support it
compositions.good_example: Hero shot of one frame on a gradient sweep, centred, with headline space above.
compositions.bad_example: Centred portrait with a person looking sideways off-frame and too much headroom.
compositions.fix: Tighten framing or move to thirds when gaze implies direction.
compositions.when_to_break: Narrative frames needing direction or look room.
compositions.aspect_ratio_notes: Ideal for 1:1 and 9:16 (UI safe); in 16:9 the sides may feel empty.
compositions.negative_space_use: Equal margins, often text above/below.
compositions.depth_layers: Background blur supports it.
ai_prompt_phrases: centred hero product shot, the glasses in the middle of the frame
compositions.ai_pitfalls: Easiest for models — the default. Risk is that every image is centred; vary deliberately.

overlay_guide.note: Focal point within 0.1 of centre.

compositions.name: Negative space
compositions.name_th: พื้นที่ว่าง
compositions.what: Large intentional empty area around a small subject.
compositions.why_it_works: Isolation raises the salience of the subject (contrast with a uniform surround, Itti1998). Emotional reading (loneliness, calm, luxury) is craft.
how_to_apply: Keep the subject small and simple
Make the empty area plain (sky, wall, sand)
Decide what the space is for (emotion or text)
compositions.good_example: Matte black titanium glasses slightly below centre on pale sand, upper third clean sky for a headline (curriculum-03).
compositions.bad_example: 'Minimal' prompt plus 'detailed, intricate' words, producing clutter.
compositions.fix: Remove busy terms, describe the empty area concretely.
compositions.when_to_break: Information-heavy posts, products needing detail.
compositions.aspect_ratio_notes: 9:16 put space top for headline; 16:9 side space; 1:1 corners.
compositions.negative_space_use: Primary — headline area or emotion.
compositions.depth_layers: Often 1-2 layers.
ai_prompt_phrases: clean negative space in the upper third for a headline, no text
minimal composition, small subject, plain empty background
compositions.ai_pitfalls: Models fill space with props; repeat 'empty' and name the surface. Never let the model write text. Outpaint to add space.

overlay_guide.note: Measure low-detail area fraction; e.g. ≥ 40% low-edge-density.

compositions.name: Frame within a frame
compositions.name_th: กรอบซ้อนกรอบ
compositions.what: A doorway, window, mirror, display case or the eyewear frame itself encloses the subject.
compositions.why_it_works: Enclosure is a Gestalt figure cue (closure, surroundedness) and adds contrast edges around the subject (Wagemans2012). Narrative meanings (secrecy, being watched) are craft (curriculum-03).
how_to_apply: Find an enclosing shape
Put the subject inside it
Keep the frame darker or out of focus
compositions.good_example: Optician seen through the cabinet's wooden doorway; or eyes framed through a pair of glasses held up.
compositions.bad_example: The inner frame is busier than the subject.
compositions.fix: Darken or blur the frame layer.
compositions.when_to_break: Open, free feelings.
compositions.aspect_ratio_notes: Works in all ratios; a vertical door suits 9:16.
compositions.negative_space_use: Frame border acts as structured space.
compositions.depth_layers: Frame usually FG, subject MG.
ai_prompt_phrases: seen through the open doorway of a glass display cabinet
her eyes framed through a pair of glasses held up to the camera
compositions.ai_pitfalls: Models merge frame and subject; use foreground/midground wording.

overlay_guide.note: Detect enclosing contour around focal point.

compositions.name: Layered depth (FG/MG/BG)
compositions.name_th: ชั้นความลึก
compositions.what: Distinct foreground, midground and background planes.
compositions.why_it_works: Pictorial depth cues — overlap, size gradient, aerial perspective, defocus — are established perception findings (Livingstone2002); layering stacks them.
how_to_apply: FG: an edge object (often blurred)
MG: the story/subject
BG: place and time
Separate by tone and focus
compositions.good_example: Blurred cabinet edge FG, optician holding tortoiseshell frames MG, hazy street BG.
compositions.bad_example: Everything equally sharp at one distance — flat.
compositions.fix: Add an FG object and atmospheric fade.
compositions.when_to_break: Flat graphic styles, flatlays.
compositions.viewing_path: FG edge → MG subject → BG context.
compositions.aspect_ratio_notes: 9:16 stack vertically; 16:9 horizontally.
compositions.negative_space_use: Blurred BG works as soft space.
compositions.depth_layers: Three explicit layers.
ai_prompt_phrases: foreground: ..., midground: ..., background: ...
blurred foreground edge, sharp subject, hazy background
compositions.ai_pitfalls: FLUX responds well to explicit FG/MG/BG (curriculum-03, BFL docs); without it models flatten.

overlay_guide.note: Use depth map (tools/depth.py) to check ≥ 3 depth clusters.

compositions.name: Subject isolation
compositions.name_th: แยกตัวแบบให้เด่น
compositions.what: Separating the subject by focus, light, colour or tone contrast.
compositions.why_it_works: Saliency is driven by local contrast in intensity, colour and orientation (Itti1998); one saturated colour among muted ones draws the eye (curriculum-03).
how_to_apply: Shallow depth of field
Light the subject brighter
Single accent colour
Clean background
compositions.good_example: Red frame sharp on a grey blurred table.
compositions.bad_example: Subject the same tone as background.
compositions.fix: Change background value or add rim light.
compositions.when_to_break: Environmental storytelling.
compositions.aspect_ratio_notes: All ratios.
compositions.negative_space_use: Muted BG becomes space.
compositions.depth_layers: Often 2 layers.
ai_prompt_phrases: shallow depth of field, the glasses sharp against a softly blurred background
the only saturated colour in the frame
compositions.ai_pitfalls: Models may add accent colours everywhere; state 'muted background'.

overlay_guide.note: Saliency peak should coincide with focal point.

compositions.name: Visual weight counterbalance
compositions.name_th: ถ่วงน้ำหนักภาพ
compositions.what: Deliberate balancing of elements by size, value, colour, text and position.
compositions.why_it_works: Arnheim1974: weight from size, colour, location, isolation; faces and text are heavy. Lever effect is theory and craft.
how_to_apply: List the heavy elements: faces, text, saturated colour, high contrast, large size, elements near the edge
Squint or blur to see masses
Move heavy elements toward centre or add a counterweight opposite
Re-check after adding HTML text, which adds weight
compositions.good_example: Bold headline block top-left (HTML) balanced by a bright frame cutout bottom-right, plain background between.
compositions.bad_example: Large red price tag beside the face pulls the eye away from the product (curriculum-03).
compositions.fix: Reduce price size/saturation, move it to a quiet corner, or give the face/product more contrast.
compositions.when_to_break: When unease or instability is the message (intentional imbalance).
compositions.focal_point_strategy: Make the heaviest element the focal point; reduce competing weights.
compositions.aspect_ratio_notes: 16:9 balance left/right; 9:16 balance top/bottom and keep weight inside the safe box; 1:1 balance on diagonals.
compositions.negative_space_use: Empty area around an element increases its weight through isolation.
compositions.depth_layers: Nearer, larger elements carry more weight; blurred BG carries little.
ai_prompt_phrases: a large dark shape on the left balanced by a small bright accent on the right
keep the right half quiet for text
compositions.ai_pitfalls: Models do not know the text that will be added; generate the image leaving the text side quiet, then balance in HTML. They also add random bright accents that steal weight — remove with inpainting or ask for a muted background.

overlay_guide.note: Saliency/contrast-weighted centroid; within ±0.08 of centre = balanced, beyond = deliberate imbalance.

compositions.name: Figure-ground
compositions.name_th: ภาพกับพื้น
compositions.what: Make the subject (figure) read instantly as separate from its background (ground) through value, colour, edge and shape contrast — or make the relationship ambiguous on purpose.
compositions.why_it_works: Core Gestalt finding: regions that are smaller, enclosed, convex, symmetric or lower in the frame tend to be seen as figure (Wertheimer1923; reviewed in Wagemans2012). Clear figure-ground lets viewers parse a thumbnail in a glance.
how_to_apply: Squint or blur the draft: the subject must remain a readable shape
Put a light subject on dark ground or vice versa (value first, colour second)
Remove tangents where subject edges touch background lines
Give dark-haired or dark-framed subjects a rim or lighter background
compositions.good_example: Black acetate frame as a crisp silhouette on a pale Timberwolf sweep; every edge readable at thumbnail size.
compositions.bad_example: Lamp post appears to grow out of a customer's head; dark frame on dark wood disappears (curriculum-03 mistake list).
compositions.fix: Shift the camera a few degrees, change background value, or add rim light so the outline separates.
compositions.when_to_break: Op-art or puzzle images where figure-ground reversal is the point; mystery frames where the subject should emerge slowly.
compositions.focal_point_strategy: The figure is the focal point; keep its strongest edge contrast at the most important part (eyes, lens).
compositions.viewing_path: Figure shape first → its internal detail → ground context.
compositions.aspect_ratio_notes: Same in all ratios; in 9:16 the platform UI overlays add a third 'layer' — keep the figure clear of it.
compositions.negative_space_use: The ground is the negative space; keep it simple in value.
compositions.depth_layers: Usually two (figure, ground); a third FG layer must not merge with the figure.
ai_prompt_phrases: the dark frames stand out as a clean silhouette against a pale plain background
strong separation between subject and background, nothing touching the outline
compositions.ai_pitfalls: Models often place background lines tangent to heads or let similar tones merge. Check a blurred/greyscale version; fix with background value words or a cutout composited in HTML over a generated background.

overlay_guide.note: Convert to greyscale, Otsu threshold; figure should form one dominant blob with mean value contrast ≥ 0.25 against ground.

compositions.name: S-curve flow
compositions.name_th: เส้นโค้งตัว S
compositions.what: A gentle S-shaped line (shoreline, path, river, draped cloth, body pose) that carries the eye through the frame in a relaxed zig-zag.
compositions.why_it_works: Gestalt good continuation makes a smooth curve read as one path (Wagemans2012). Its 'grace' and calm associations are craft (Artistic), not measured.
how_to_apply: Start the curve at a bottom corner or edge
Let it swing across the frame at least twice
End it on or near the subject
Keep the curve the smoothest, most continuous line in the image
compositions.good_example: Hua Hin water line curving from the lower right, across the middle, to a woman in sunglasses on the upper left third.
compositions.bad_example: The curve exits the side of the frame and the subject sits off the path.
compositions.fix: Reframe so the curve terminates at the subject, or move the subject onto the curve.
compositions.when_to_break: Rigid geometric, architectural or tech themes; urgent messages where a straight diagonal is stronger.
compositions.focal_point_strategy: Subject at the end (or the last bend) of the S.
compositions.viewing_path: Entry corner → first bend → second bend → subject.
compositions.aspect_ratio_notes: Natural in 9:16 and 4:5 (vertical S); in 16:9 flatten to a horizontal S; 1:1 fits one bend plus end.
compositions.negative_space_use: Calm areas inside the bends; good places for small text.
compositions.depth_layers: A receding S (road into distance) adds strong depth.
ai_prompt_phrases: a winding S-shaped path leads from the bottom of the frame to the person
gently curving shoreline sweeping toward the figure
compositions.ai_pitfalls: 'S-curve composition' is weak in prompts; name the concrete element that curves and where it starts/ends. Use a sketch with img2img for exact shape.

overlay_guide.note: Example S control points (Catmull-Rom); mirror horizontally as needed.

compositions.name: Repetition / rhythm
compositions.name_th: การซ้ำและจังหวะ
compositions.what: Repeated shapes, colours or objects at regular or progressive intervals, creating visual rhythm.
compositions.why_it_works: Similarity and proximity cause repeated elements to group into a pattern (Gestalt; Wagemans2012). Perceived 'rhythm' and its calming or energetic effect is craft.
how_to_apply: Repeat one element type (frames, shelves, arches)
Choose interval: regular = calm, accelerating = energy
Let repetition recede for depth
Plan one focal point (often a pattern_break)
compositions.good_example: Wall of identical display shelves receding diagonally, each with a pair of frames, the nearest one sharp.
compositions.bad_example: Flat even grid with no focal point; the eye wanders and leaves.
compositions.fix: Add size progression, perspective, or one different element.
compositions.when_to_break: Single hero product with negative space; emotional portraits.
compositions.focal_point_strategy: Nearest/sharpest repeat or the odd one out.
compositions.viewing_path: Along the row → to the end or the break.
compositions.aspect_ratio_notes: 16:9 and 21:9 suit horizontal rows; 9:16 vertical stacks; 1:1 grids.
compositions.negative_space_use: Intervals between repeats are rhythmic space.
compositions.depth_layers: Receding repetition is a strong size-gradient depth cue.
ai_prompt_phrases: a long row of identical eyeglass frames on wooden shelves receding into the distance
repeating arches creating rhythm
compositions.ai_pitfalls: Models make repeated items inconsistent (different shapes, melted copies). For exact repetition, generate one item and repeat cutouts in HTML.

overlay_guide.note: Autocorrelation/FFT peak along x or y indicates repetition; report interval in normalised units.

compositions.name: Scale contrast
compositions.name_th: ความต่างของขนาด
compositions.what: Pair something very large with something very small to show scale, power or vulnerability.
compositions.why_it_works: Size difference is salient and also a depth cue (familiar size; Livingstone2002). Meanings (grandeur, loneliness, power) are craft; size/height in frame = power is a film convention (curriculum-03).
how_to_apply: Pick a known-size reference (person, hand)
Make the size ratio extreme (≥ 1:10)
Give the small element contrast so it is not lost
Keep the large element simple
compositions.good_example: Tiny figure walking across the bridge of a giant pair of glasses on a white plane (surreal promo).
compositions.bad_example: Elements of similar sizes scattered with no hierarchy.
compositions.fix: Enlarge the hero or shrink the reference; remove mid-sized clutter.
compositions.when_to_break: Accurate product scale is needed (size guides, fitting info).
compositions.focal_point_strategy: Usually the small element (contrast-boosted) or the large element's detail.
compositions.viewing_path: Large mass → small figure → back to large.
compositions.aspect_ratio_notes: 9:16 shows height/vertical scale; 21:9 and 16:9 landscape scale.
compositions.negative_space_use: Large empty area emphasises smallness.
compositions.depth_layers: Small far figure vs huge near object exaggerates depth.
ai_prompt_phrases: a tiny person standing next to giant eyeglasses, extreme scale contrast
small lone figure dwarfed by a huge landscape
compositions.ai_pitfalls: Models normalise sizes; state the ratio in words ('the person is no taller than the lens'). Compose large/small layers separately and scale in HTML for control.

overlay_guide.note: Ratio of bounding-box areas of largest and smallest salient objects; ≥ 10 = strong contrast.

compositions.name: Pattern break
compositions.name_th: แหวกแบบแผน
compositions.what: One element differs (colour, orientation, size, state) within an otherwise uniform pattern.
compositions.why_it_works: Visual search 'pop-out': a single feature singleton in a homogeneous field is detected quickly, consistent with saliency models (Itti1998).
how_to_apply: Build a clean uniform pattern
Change exactly one feature of one element
Place the odd element off-centre (thirds) for interest
Keep everything else identical
compositions.good_example: Grid of black frames with one Peach-coloured frame on the upper-right power point.
compositions.bad_example: Several 'special' elements competing; or noisy pattern so the break does not pop.
compositions.fix: Reduce to one break and make the pattern more uniform.
compositions.when_to_break: When calm repetition itself is the message.
compositions.viewing_path: Immediate jump to the break → pattern for context.
compositions.aspect_ratio_notes: All; dense grids suit 1:1 and 4:5.
compositions.negative_space_use: The uniform pattern acts as a textured ground.
compositions.depth_layers: Usually flat; works in perspective too.
ai_prompt_phrases: rows of identical black eyeglass frames, one single bright peach frame among them
everything identical except one
compositions.ai_pitfalls: Models scatter variations and miscount. Best built in HTML from one cutout repeated + one recoloured.

overlay_guide.note: Feature-outlier detection (colour/orientation z-score > 3 for exactly one object).

compositions.name: Odd grouping (rule of odds)
compositions.name_th: จัดกลุ่มเลขคี่
compositions.what: Group objects in odd numbers (3, 5) so one can sit in the middle and the group reads as a unit.
compositions.why_it_works: Craft rule (Artistic). No strong evidence that odd numbers are preferred; the useful part is avoiding a 50/50 split between two equal items and giving the group a centre.
how_to_apply: Group 3 (or 5) items close together (proximity)
Vary size/height/depth
Make one the hero
Avoid perfect line-ups
compositions.good_example: Three frames on a stone: hero front-centre, two behind at different heights.
compositions.bad_example: Two identical frames side by side, attention split down the middle.
compositions.fix: Add a third smaller prop or make one of the two clearly dominant.
compositions.when_to_break: Pairs for comparison (before/after, his/hers); data/grid layouts.
compositions.viewing_path: Hero → second → third → back to hero.
compositions.aspect_ratio_notes: All; triangle grouping fits 1:1 and 4:5.
compositions.negative_space_use: Space around the group frames it as one unit.
compositions.depth_layers: Stagger items front/back.
ai_prompt_phrases: three pairs of glasses grouped together on a stone, one in front and two behind
compositions.ai_pitfalls: Models often generate the wrong count (2 or 4). Verify; place cutouts in HTML for exact counts.

overlay_guide.note: Count salient objects; flag even counts of equal-sized items.

compositions.name: Z-pattern layout
compositions.name_th: รูปแบบตัว Z
compositions.what: For sparse graphic layouts, place elements along a Z: top-left → top-right → diagonal → bottom-left → bottom-right.
compositions.why_it_works: Craft/design heuristic based on left-to-right, top-to-bottom reading habits (English and Thai both read left-to-right). Treat as a layout convention, not proven gaze law.
how_to_apply: Logo or hook top-left
Headline top-right or across
Image across the diagonal
CTA or price bottom-right (inside the safe zone)
compositions.good_example: 1:1 promo: partner logo top-left, headline top-right, glasses on the diagonal, 'แชทเลย' CTA bottom-right.
compositions.bad_example: CTA top-left before the viewer knows the offer.
compositions.fix: Reorder elements along reading order; end with the action.
compositions.when_to_break: Image-led emotional posts; centred hero layouts; 9:16 where bottom-right is covered by UI.
compositions.focal_point_strategy: Image at the diagonal, CTA as final stop.
compositions.aspect_ratio_notes: Best 1:1, 4:5, web banners; 9:16 bottom-right is platform UI — move CTA up into the safe box (x 65-950, y 270-1250 on 1080×1920, curriculum-03).
compositions.negative_space_use: Empty corridors between Z strokes keep it scannable.
compositions.depth_layers: Mostly flat graphic layers.
ai_prompt_phrases: plain background with clean empty areas in the top right and bottom right corners for text
product placed on a diagonal from lower left to upper right
compositions.ai_pitfalls: Never let the model write the text; generate the image with empty zones and set text in HTML.

overlay_guide.note: Z path; check that key elements sit near its vertices.

compositions.name: F-pattern layout
compositions.name_th: รูปแบบตัว F
compositions.what: For text-heavy slides: strong headline across the top, sub-points left-aligned beneath, so a scanning eye reads the left edge and the first words of each line.
compositions.why_it_works: Craft/UX convention for scanning text; reading-pattern research exists for web pages but is outside this brief's keys, so it is labelled craft here. Left alignment gives a single strong edge (MullerBrockmann1981 grid logic).
how_to_apply: Headline full-width at top
Left-align bullets
Front-load key words
Image or icon on the right, not interrupting the left edge
compositions.good_example: Carousel tip slide: headline top, 3 left-aligned tips, small frame cutout bottom-right.
compositions.bad_example: Centred multi-line paragraphs with ragged both sides.
compositions.fix: Left-align and shorten lines; bold the first words.
compositions.when_to_break: Image-led or single-message posts; quote images (centre may be right).
compositions.viewing_path: Across the top → down the left → short horizontal sweeps.
compositions.aspect_ratio_notes: 4:5 and 1:1 carousels; 16:9 slides; in 9:16 keep it inside the safe box.
compositions.negative_space_use: Right side breathing room or image area.
compositions.depth_layers: Flat; background image should be quiet behind text.
ai_prompt_phrases: soft plain background with a large empty area on the left for text
subtle illustration in the lower right corner only
compositions.ai_pitfalls: Text belongs in the HTML layer; ask the model only for a quiet background with space.

overlay_guide.note: F strokes; text block left edge near x=0.08.

compositions.name: Flatlay grid
compositions.name_th: จัดวางมุมบนเป็นกริด
compositions.what: Camera straight down (90°) over objects arranged on an aligned grid or knolling layout.
compositions.why_it_works: Alignment and proximity grouping make items read as an organised set (Gestalt; Wagemans2012); grid structure is a design craft (MullerBrockmann1981).
how_to_apply: Shoot/request true top-down
Align items to a grid with equal gutters
Rotate items to 0°/90° (knolling) or a consistent angle
Choose one hero larger or central
compositions.good_example: Frame, case, cleaning cloth and lens card on a Snow background, equal spacing, hero frame centre-top.
compositions.bad_example: Slight perspective tilt and random angles look careless.
compositions.fix: Exact 90° camera; straighten items; consistent gutters.
compositions.when_to_break: Lifestyle warmth wanted (loose scatter, hands entering).
compositions.focal_point_strategy: Hero item largest or at centre/upper third.
compositions.aspect_ratio_notes: 1:1 and 4:5 ideal; 9:16 stack as a column; 16:9 rows.
compositions.negative_space_use: Gutters and margins are the space; generous margins read premium.
compositions.depth_layers: Flat; only contact shadows give depth.
ai_prompt_phrases: top-down flat lay, objects neatly arranged in a grid on a plain light background, soft even shadows
knolling layout, everything aligned at right angles
compositions.ai_pitfalls: Models tilt the camera and warp objects. Prefer real cutouts arranged in HTML over a generated surface texture.

overlay_guide.note: Check object centres snap to grid within ±0.03.

compositions.name: Over the shoulder
compositions.name_th: มุมข้ามไหล่
compositions.what: Camera behind one character's shoulder, which occupies a blurred edge of the frame, looking at the other character or object.
compositions.why_it_works: Film grammar craft for dialogue and POV (Block2008, bibliographic; curriculum-03 GUIDE eyeline). Puts the viewer inside the scene.
how_to_apply: Shoulder/head as dark blurred FG on one side (~1/4 of frame)
Other face on the opposite third
Respect the 180° line
Eyeline toward the shoulder
compositions.good_example: Customer's shoulder FG left, optician MG right third adjusting frames, looking at her.
compositions.bad_example: Shoulder fills half the frame and the face is cramped against the edge.
compositions.fix: Reduce shoulder to a quarter; open more look room.
compositions.when_to_break: Single-subject product shots; when isolation is the point.
compositions.aspect_ratio_notes: 16:9 natural; 9:16 crop shoulder to the bottom corner; 1:1 tight.
compositions.negative_space_use: Shoulder is a dark mass framing the face.
compositions.depth_layers: FG shoulder, MG face, BG shop.
ai_prompt_phrases: over-the-shoulder shot from behind the customer's blurred shoulder, the optician facing camera on the right third
compositions.ai_pitfalls: Models often show both faces or place the camera in front; describe whose back is to camera and its blur. A rough sketch + img2img helps.

overlay_guide.note: Shoulder zone left; face near the right-upper power point (mirror as needed).

compositions.name: Dominant foreground
compositions.name_th: ฉากหน้าเด่น
compositions.what: A large, near object fills the lower or side portion of the frame with the scene extending deep behind it (wide lens, close distance).
compositions.why_it_works: Relative size and perspective convergence are established depth cues (Livingstone2002); exaggerating the near element amplifies depth. Visual drama is craft.
how_to_apply: Use a wide lens (16-28 mm) close to the near object
Place it low or to one side
Keep a clear line to the background
Focus near or deep
compositions.good_example: Sunglasses huge in the lower foreground on beach sand, sharp; sea and tiny figures behind.
compositions.bad_example: Foreground object blocks the subject or is an unrelated blur.
compositions.fix: Lower/shift the FG so the background story stays visible.
compositions.when_to_break: Flat graphic styles; accurate product proportion (wide-angle distorts).
compositions.focal_point_strategy: FG hero object, BG supports context.
compositions.aspect_ratio_notes: 9:16 strong (FG bottom, BG top); 16:9 FG in a lower corner.
compositions.negative_space_use: Sky/BG area above becomes text space.
compositions.depth_layers: Exaggerated FG + distant BG, MG optional.
ai_prompt_phrases: wide-angle close-up, the sunglasses large in the lower foreground, the beach stretching far behind
low camera, huge foreground object, deep background
compositions.ai_pitfalls: Models shrink the FG object to mid-size; specify 'fills the bottom third' and lens mm. Product shape may distort — use a real cutout for the product.

overlay_guide.note: FG occupies the bottom ~40%; check depth map near-plane fraction.

compositions.name: Low horizon
compositions.name_th: เส้นขอบฟ้าต่ำ
compositions.what: Horizon placed low (around the lower third or below) so sky dominates.
compositions.why_it_works: Craft: emphasis follows area — a big sky stresses space, weather, freedom. Horizon placement on a third is a thirds convention (curriculum-03).
how_to_apply: Put horizon at y ≈ 0.67-0.85
Make the sky interesting or plain for text
Keep the horizon level
Small subject on the horizon line
compositions.good_example: Hua Hin dusk: thin strip of beach at the bottom, vast gradient sky, small figure in sunglasses.
compositions.bad_example: Low horizon with a blank grey sky and nothing to say.
compositions.fix: Use the sky for text or colour story, or raise the horizon.
compositions.when_to_break: When ground detail matters; dull skies.
compositions.focal_point_strategy: Subject on or just above the horizon line.
compositions.aspect_ratio_notes: 9:16 ideal (sky as headline area, keep below top 14% UI); 16:9 landscape; 1:1 works.
compositions.negative_space_use: Sky = negative space / headline zone.
compositions.depth_layers: Ground FG thin, sky BG.
ai_prompt_phrases: low horizon in the bottom fifth of the frame, vast open sky above
huge sky, small figure on the horizon
compositions.ai_pitfalls: Models centre horizons; give explicit fraction. Outpaint upward to add sky.

overlay_guide.note: Detected horizon y should be ≥ 0.62; tilt ≤ 0.5°.

compositions.name: High horizon
compositions.name_th: เส้นขอบฟ้าสูง
compositions.what: Horizon placed high (upper third or above) so ground/sea dominates.
compositions.why_it_works: Craft: emphasis on terrain, path or subject on the ground; reduces sky distraction.
how_to_apply: Horizon at y ≈ 0.15-0.33
Fill ground with texture or leading lines
Subject in the lower area
Keep level
compositions.good_example: Sand ripples and footprints leading to sunglasses lying near the bottom, sea a thin band at top.
compositions.bad_example: High horizon with featureless ground.
compositions.fix: Add texture, lines or a subject on the ground.
compositions.when_to_break: Dramatic skies.
compositions.focal_point_strategy: Subject in the lower or middle ground.
compositions.aspect_ratio_notes: 9:16 good for paths; keep horizon below the top UI zone (≈ 14%).
compositions.negative_space_use: Smooth ground areas.
compositions.depth_layers: Ground receding gives depth.
ai_prompt_phrases: high horizon near the top of the frame, mostly sand in view
looking down a path, horizon in the upper fifth
compositions.ai_pitfalls: Models centre horizons; specify the fraction and camera tilt down.

overlay_guide.note: Detected horizon y should be ≤ 0.38.

compositions.name: Vignette / tunnel
compositions.name_th: ขอบมืดและอุโมงค์
compositions.what: Edges darker or enclosed (arch, foliage, corridor, lens vignette) funnelling attention to a bright centre.
compositions.why_it_works: Brightness contrast and enclosure pull attention to the lit centre (saliency, Itti1998; enclosure as figure cue, Wagemans2012). Strength of effect is craft-tuned.
how_to_apply: Darken edges 0.5-1.5 stops
Keep the subject in the brightest area
Use real tunnels or arches for depth
Subtle in ads, strong in drama
compositions.good_example: Corridor of the old shop at night, dark walls, bright pair of glasses at the far end.
compositions.bad_example: Heavy post vignette on a bright product image, looking dated.
compositions.fix: Reduce strength or use real light falloff.
compositions.when_to_break: High-key clean posts; flatlays.
compositions.aspect_ratio_notes: Circular vignette in 1:1; elliptical in 16:9; in 9:16 darken top/bottom lightly — UI already covers them.
compositions.negative_space_use: Dark edges are quiet space.
compositions.depth_layers: Tunnel gives FG to BG depth.
ai_prompt_phrases: dark vignette around the edges, light focused on the centre
looking down a dark tunnel toward a bright opening
compositions.ai_pitfalls: Models can produce over-strong vignettes or none; better added in HTML/CSS (radial gradient) so it is controllable.

overlay_guide.note: Compare mean luminance inside r=0.35 vs outside r=0.5.

compositions.name: Split screen
compositions.name_th: แบ่งจอ
compositions.what: Frame divided into two (or more) panels or halves showing contrast, comparison or simultaneity.
compositions.why_it_works: Common-region grouping (Gestalt, Wagemans2012) separates each half into its own unit, inviting comparison. Narrative use is film/comic craft (McCloud1993).
how_to_apply: Divide with a clear line/gap
Match layout/scale on both sides for comparison
Vary only the compared variable
Label in HTML
compositions.good_example: Left: blurred view without glasses; right: sharp view with the same framing.
compositions.bad_example: Two unrelated images with different framing, so the comparison is unclear.
compositions.fix: Same camera, same subject position; change one variable only.
compositions.when_to_break: Single-message hero posts.
compositions.viewing_path: Left (before) → right (after), or top → bottom in 9:16.
compositions.aspect_ratio_notes: 16:9 split left/right; 9:16 split top/bottom; 1:1 either.
compositions.negative_space_use: Gutter between halves.
compositions.depth_layers: Each half has its own layers.
ai_prompt_phrases: generate each half separately with identical framing
compositions.ai_pitfalls: Models handle split screens badly (bleed between halves). Generate halves separately (same seed/prompt with one change) and assemble in HTML.
